hrrRisk: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome
incidence: About 66% of long-duration crew show at least one early sign.

detect.label: NASA clinical SANS criteria
detect.criterion: Change in total peripapillary retinal thickness by OCT: 20 um or more is an early indication; 55 um or more and/or Frisen grade 1 or higher is clinically concerning.

treat.text: Stop vision-critical tasks if there is a visual deficit.
Run the OCT and vision tests; review cabin CO2, sleep and fluid shift.
Apply only a pre-approved mechanical countermeasure.
Loss of visual field or acuity: escalate to the flight surgeon.

cautions: Lower body negative pressure is not a validated SANS treatment.
efficacy: LBNP for SANS: NR as validated clinical efficacy; the HRR gap is open.

verify.criterion: Retinal thickness stable or reduced, no Frisen progression, visual field and refraction within the individual baseline.

condition: Bone mineral density loss and fracture risk
hrrRisk: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone
incidence: Not an acute incidence: typical loss of 0.8-1.2 %/month (DXA) at spine and hip.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Trend of bone density, resorption markers and loading adherence against the crew member's own baseline. Standard Measures collects these data but publishes no yellow or red threshold.

treat.text: Prescribed resistive exercise programme (ARED).
Nutrition and vitamin D per the medical plan.
Bisphosphonate only as part of a pre-authorized individual protocol.

efficacy: ARED: mean loss about 1.0 to 0.3-0.5 %/month; alendronate plus exercise (n=4): femoral neck -1.1 to -0.2 %/month.

verify.criterion: Bone density trend stabilized; resorption markers and urinary calcium not rising; loading sessions completed.

condition: Loss of muscle mass, strength and fitness
hrrRisk: Risk of Reduced Cardiorespiratory and Musculoskeletal Fitness
incidence: Calf volume -10 to -16% and thigh -4 to -7% in historical ISS data.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Strength, muscle volume and exercise load against the crew member's own baseline and the operational task standards.

treat.text: Prescribed resistance and aerobic programme.
Progress loads only within the protocol.

efficacy: Current countermeasures reduce but do not eliminate losses; some astronauts keep 10-15% deficits.

verify.criterion: Strength, muscle volume, aerobic capacity and functional task back in the individual target range.

incidence: About 30% after short flights; up to 83% after long-duration flights.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Heart-rate and systolic-pressure response on standing or tilt against baseline. The Standard Measure tilt test (80 degrees, up to 15 minutes or presyncope) defines the measurement, not an alert threshold.

treat.text: Fluid and salt loading per the pre-approved protocol.
Wear the compression garments.
Lower body negative pressure when the protocol calls for it.

efficacy: Salt and water: heart-rate response reduced 29%. Compression: heart-rate rise 11 vs 21 bpm and systolic +2 vs -9 mmHg.

verify.criterion: Stand or tilt test completed without presyncope; systolic pressure sustained; heart rate near baseline.

incidence: 19 of 49 astronauts (about 38.7%) reported headache in an ISS series.

detect.label: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2 [V2 6004]
detect.criterion: One-hour average ppCO2 of 3 mmHg or less. A sustained rise against the local baseline, or headache and fatigue with it, counts as early warning.

treat.text: Increase CO2 scrubbing and ventilation.
Leave the CO2 pocket.
Reduce metabolic load as the procedure allows.
Analgesia only per the medical checklist.

cautions: 2.5 mmHg as a 7-day mean is an epidemiological relation, not a NASA red limit.
efficacy: Estimated headache risk under 1% at a 7-day mean below 2.5 mmHg; odds about double per +1 mmHg.

verify.criterion: ppCO2 at or below 3 mmHg and falling; headache and fatigue resolved; heart rate and breathing at baseline.

condition: Altered immune response and latent virus reactivation
hrrRisk: Risk of Adverse Health Event Due to Altered Immune Response
incidence: VZV reactivation in about 50% of astronauts in one long-duration series.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Temperature, symptoms, skin findings and available blood markers against the crew member's own baseline. Standard Measures records immune status but sets no clinical threshold.

treat.text: Monitor symptoms, temperature, skin and the blood markers available.
Isolation and hygiene measures.
Antiviral only if pre-authorized for a defined diagnosis.

efficacy: Universal preventive pharmacological countermeasure: NR; research remains open.

verify.criterion: Afebrile, symptoms resolved, markers back in the individual range, no progression of rash or infection.

condition: Sleep loss, circadian disruption and cognitive decline
hrrRisk: Risk of Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules
incidence: No single clinical incidence. Standard Measures (n=19): 7.33 +/- 1.16 h in flight vs 7.87 +/- 1.10 h before.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Sleep duration and efficiency, vigilance testing and subjective alertness against the individual envelope. The PVT is validated as a measure, but no NASA alert threshold exists.

treat.text: Reschedule sleep and work periods.
Use the circadian lighting schedule.
Reduce workload per the plan.
Sleep medication only within the medical protocol.

efficacy: Lighting and schedule are active countermeasures; a universal clinical percentage is NR.

verify.criterion: Vigilance and cognition back inside the individual envelope; sleep duration, efficiency and subjective alertness recovered.

condition: Radiation exposure: solar particle events and cumulative dose
incidence: Human incidence for exploration: NR. Observed environment: about 1.84 mSv/day in transit and 0.7 mSv/day on the Martian surface.

detect.label: Program-defined mission budget (NR by default; not a NASA daily limit)
detect.criterion: Solar particle event detected from the flux of protons at 10 MeV or more; cumulative dose, its rate of increase and the margin against a configurable mission budget.

treat.text: Solar particle event: move to the storm shelter.
Reconfigure mass and water as shielding.
Keep the personal dosimeter on continuously.

cautions: Radioprotective drugs are not for autonomous use: no experimental radioprotector is self-administered.
efficacy: Common shielding: about 50% dose reduction for SPE and 7% for GCR. AstroRad: 58.2% and 36.9% modeled for two historical events.

verify.criterion: Dose rate falls after sheltering; cumulative dose stays within the budget; no acute radiation syndrome.

condition: Adverse medical conditions without real-time ground support
incidence: No percentage: the Integrated Medical Model gives expected events per simulated mission.

detect.label: Depends on the condition (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Vital signs and objective findings for the suspected condition. Standard Measures must not be read as a diagnosis.

treat.text: Follow the medical checklist with the Crew Medical Officer.
Use the differential algorithm and the resources on board.

Arrhythmia, sepsis, airway compromise, shock, severe toxic exposure, major trauma, neurological deficit or SANS with loss of vision: emergency mode, pre-approved protocols only, and request the medical link as soon as communications allow.

cautions: In emergency mode the software guides approved protocols; it does not try treatments or change doses outside the authorized medical order.
efficacy: Decision support, not a substitute for the Crew Medical Officer; no single published efficacy figure.

verify.criterion: Vital signs and objective findings normalize; the condition leaves the escalation criteria; no functional decline.

condition: Skin rash, respiratory infection and minor trauma
hrrRisk: Hostile closed environment: common in-flight conditions
incidence: Simulated, not observed: rash 9.83, respiratory infection 3.46 and skin abrasion 9.86 events per simulated mission.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Temperature, pain, lesion extent, SpO2 and breathing against the crew member's own baseline.

treat.text: Examination, hygiene and wound care per the medical checklist.
Medication and procedures only per the approved protocol.

verify.criterion: Temperature, pain, lesion extent, SpO2 and breathing back to baseline; no systemic progression.

hrrRisk: Risk of Inadequate Food and Nutrition
incidence: Not in the research report matrix. NASA lists it as a spaceflight risk without a published incidence.

detect.label: Individual baseline (not a NASA limit)
detect.criterion: Energy intake and blood glucose against the crew member's own requirement and baseline. NASA publishes no alert threshold.

treat.text: Add planned snacks and energy-dense items from the pantry.
Review the menu with the Crew Medical Officer.

cautions: This rule was added by the project to cover existing indicators; it is not part of the research report.

verify.criterion: Energy intake back at the individual target; glucose and body mass stable.
